sources.heading: Where do the numbers come from?
sources.planHeading: How the plan is worked out
sources.footnote: Sources: Energinet (Energi Data Service) and the Nord Pool power exchange. GreenHour is a private project, not a public authority, and its plans are suggestions, not advice.

price.title: Electricity price
price.text: The Nord Pool spot price for every quarter of an hour in your price area. GreenHour fetches it every hour from Energinet's Energi Data Service and converts it from DKK per MWh to DKK per kWh.

co2.title: CO₂ per kWh
co2.text: How much CO₂ the electricity in your price area emits. Energinet measures it every 5 minutes, and GreenHour averages it for each quarter of an hour. The rest of today is based on Energinet's forecast.

windows.title: Cheapest 2 hours, most expensive time and average
windows.text: Worked out by GreenHour from the spot prices above.

tariff.title: Grid tariff, taxes and VAT
tariff.text: Not included, because the grid tariff depends on your grid company. Most grid companies charge the most between 17:00 and 21:00, so moving usage away from those hours usually saves more than GreenHour shows.

usage.title: Energy per run
usage.text: Power × run time for the appliance, as entered under My home. GreenHour assumes the same power for the whole run, although most appliances use the most while heating up.

planData.title: Price and CO₂
planData.text: The same Energinet spot prices and CO₂ figures as on the prices page, without grid tariffs, taxes and VAT.

bestStart.title: Best start time and saving
bestStart.text: GreenHour tries every quarter of an hour in your window as a start time and picks the cheapest, the one with the least CO₂, or a balance of the two. The saving is the difference from starting as early as you allowed.
